title: Chicken and Ham Pie
subtitle: Tender chicken and gammon in a creamy sauce under a golden shortcrust
excerpt: Chicken and ham pie combines two reliable British pie fillings into one: poached chicken and chopped gammon in a cream and mustard sauce, enclosed in a full shortcrust shell. The gammon adds salt and a gentle smokiness, while the mustard lifts the cream without dominating. It is one of the most crowd-pleasing pies in British cooking.
sourceNotes: The combination of chicken and ham or gammon in a pastry shell is a long-established British picnic and celebration pie. Cold chicken and ham pie is a staple of the British deli counter.

recipe.freezeNotes: Bake, cool completely, wrap tightly, and freeze. Defrost overnight and serve cold, or reheat at 160°C fan for 20 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bake a day ahead and serve cold. This pie is excellent cold and holds its shape when sliced.

content.text: Chicken and ham pie is a British classic that works hot from the oven or cold from the fridge. The gammon brings its own salt, so season the sauce carefully at the end rather than at the beginning. A full shortcrust shell, base and lid, gives the pie enough structure to slice cleanly when cold.
Poach {{chicken-breast}} chicken breasts in {{stock-chicken}} of chicken stock for 15 minutes until cooked through. Lift out, cool slightly, and cut into large chunks. Reserve the stock.

In a wide pan, melt {{unsalted-butter}} of butter. Cook {{leek}} sliced leeks over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft. Stir in {{plain-flour}} of flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the warm reserved stock, then {{double-cream}} of double cream. Simmer for 5 minutes until thick. Add {{wholegrain-mustard}} of wholegrain mustard and the thyme leaves. Season carefully: the gammon adds salt. Stir in the chicken chunks and the diced gammon. Leave to cool completely.

Heat the oven to 190°C fan. Roll out two-thirds of the pastry to line a 23 cm deep pie dish. Lay the pastry into the dish, press into the edges, and trim, leaving 1 cm overhang. Blind-bake with baking paper and beans for 15 minutes.

Fill the case with the cooled filling. Roll the remaining pastry for the lid. Brush the rim with beaten egg, lay the lid, and seal. Crimp the edges. Cut a steam hole in the centre and brush all over with beaten egg. Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until deep golden.
Rest for 10 minutes before slicing if serving hot. For a cold pie, leave to cool completely in the dish before turning out.

items.cause: The filling was warm when it went in, or the base was not blind-baked.
items.fix: Always cool the filling completely before adding it to the pastry. The blind-bake sets the base and prevents it absorbing the sauce.

items.cause: Cooked gammon is salty; the sauce was also salted without tasting.
items.fix: Taste the sauce before seasoning and add no extra salt until you have accounted for what the gammon brings.

items.symptom: The lid pastry sinks into the filling
items.cause: The filling was too warm, softening the pastry before it could set.
items.fix: The filling must be cold and firm before the lid goes on. A cold, thick sauce will support the pastry as it bakes.

items.symptom: The pie is difficult to slice when cold
items.cause: The sauce was too loose and ran into the pastry.
items.fix: The sauce needs to be very thick before the filling cools , thick enough to barely fall off a spoon. It firms further as it cools.

content.text: Chicken and ham pie is a fixture of British deli counters, farm shops, and celebration tables. Served cold, it slices cleanly and travels well, making it a long-standing choice for picnics and buffets. Hot, with a jug of gravy and some greens, it is a proper main course that will feed six without complaint.
